title: Austin Budget, Community Education & Lawsuit
summary:
*   An intensive work session was held to discuss the city's operating and capital budgets, including reviews for departments like Building Inspection and Environmental services, and a Human Resources compensation study.
*   A public hearing was conducted to gather community input on local education initiatives.
*   Private executive discussions covered sensitive topics such as potential land acquisitions and ongoing litigation against Houston Lighting and Power.

Mayor Cooksey called to order the special called meeting of the Council, noting the

WORKSESSION
-
OPERATING & CAPITAL BUDGET
Council held a worksession on Operating and Capital Budget. Departments heard were General
Service, Building Inspection, Environmental, and the Human Resources report on the
Compensation Study. Department heads explained their budgets.
Mayor Cooksey announced the worksession would continue on August 27, 1987 at 9:00 a.m. No
report was presented on Residual Value Bond Program, and Council was told the report on
AIDS would be presented on Tuesday, September 1, 1987.
EXECUTIVE SESSION
Mayor Cooksey announced Council would enter into executive session pursuant to Article
6252-17, Texas Revised Civil Statutes Annotated to discuss matters of land acquisition,
litigation and for personnel matters. No final action, decision or vote by the City
Council will be taken on any subject or matter unless specifically listed on the agenda
for this meeting. 1. Pending Litigation Section 2, Paragraph e, a. City of Austin v.
Houston Lighting and Power. Council recessed for executive session at 6:00 p.m. and
resumed its recessed meeting at 6:30 p.m. -

Mayor Cooksey opened the public hearing set for 6 p.m. on Community Education. He had to
